sources.entry: mako - Hyperfast and lightweight templating for the Python platform.

summary.one_liner: Mako is a Python template library that compiles non-XML template syntax into Python modules for fast rendering.
summary.what_it_does: Mako is a template library written in Python that uses a non-XML syntax. According to the README, templates compile into Python modules to improve performance. The README says its syntax and API draw on ideas from Django templates, Cheetah, Myghty, and Genshi. It supports componentized layout and inheritance, and it keeps close ties to Python calling and scoping semantics. The README's example shows Python-style control lines (% for / % endfor) and ${...} expression substitution. The README points to external documentation and does not describe further details in the text itself.
use_cases: rendering dynamic text or report templates
building componentized page layouts with inheritance
server-side page templating in Python web apps
notable: Templates compile into Python modules for performance
Non-XML syntax with Python control lines and ${} expressions
Syntax and API borrow ideas from Django templates, Cheetah, Myghty, and Genshi
caveats: The README is brief and defers detailed documentation to an external site
No installation or run instructions are given in the README
